questions.q: According to this lesson, what is a dbt project from Git's point of view?
options: Just files — SQL and YAML in a folder, no special version-control system required
A binary format that needs a dbt-specific version control tool
Something that cannot be version-controlled at all
A database object, not a set of files
questions.explain: A dbt project is nothing but models, schema.yml files, macros, and config — plain text files, so ordinary Git applies directly.

questions.q: What does dbt Cloud's IDE 'Commit Changes' modal actually do underneath?
options: Runs a real git commit against a real repository, just triggered from a modal instead of a terminal
Saves the file locally with no Git involvement at all
Publishes the model directly to production with no history
Deletes the previous version of the file permanently
questions.explain: The modal is a convenience layer over ordinary Git — the underlying commit and history are the same as running git commit from a terminal.

questions.q: Why does per-developer branching matter more in a dbt project than in many other codebases?
options: dbt Cloud's dev environment runs each branch's models into its own schema, so simultaneous developers don't collide
dbt refuses to run at all unless every developer shares one branch
Branches have no effect on where models get built
It doesn't matter more — it's identical to any other codebase
questions.explain: Each developer's branch builds into a schema scoped to that branch, which is what lets a whole team develop against the same warehouse without stomping on each other's tables.

questions.q: What is a dbt Cloud 'managed repository'?
options: A Git repo dbt Cloud hosts for you, for projects that don't already have one on GitHub/GitLab/Azure DevOps
A repository that only Bill Green's admin account can access
A repository that cannot be committed to
A special non-Git storage format unique to dbt
questions.explain: It's an actual Git repository dbt Cloud hosts, for projects that need one — otherwise you connect your own from GitHub, GitLab, or Azure DevOps.

questions.q: Which Git/GitHub course concept does this lesson say maps directly onto opening a change for review in a dbt project?
options: Pull requests — opened the same way, whether dbt Cloud creates it or you do it directly in GitHub
There is no equivalent — dbt has no review process
Only a database administrator can approve dbt changes
Forking the entire warehouse
questions.explain: Pull requests work exactly as covered in the Git/GitHub/CI-CD course — dbt Cloud can create the PR for you, or you can do it directly in GitHub.
